title: Classifying triangles and quadrilaterals
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Not all triangles are the same, and neither are four-sided shapes. We sort them into families by their sides and angles.
Triangles are named by their sides: equilateral (3 equal sides), isosceles (2 equal sides), scalene (no equal sides).

steps: A triangle has all three sides the same length.
So it is an equilateral triangle.

blocks.prompt: A triangle with all three sides equal is called ___.
blocks.explain: Equilateral means all sides are equal.
blocks.rule: Name a triangle by its sides: equilateral (3 equal), isosceles (2 equal), scalene (none equal).

practiceItems.prompt: a triangle with exactly 2 equal sides
a triangle with no equal sides
the number of sides on any triangle

blocks.content: A quadrilateral is any shape with exactly four straight sides — squares, rectangles and rhombuses are all quadrilaterals.

blocks.question: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
blocks.explain: 'Quad' means four, so a quadrilateral has four sides.
blocks.rule: A quadrilateral is any shape with exactly four straight sides.

practiceItems.prompt: a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides and 4 right angles
a quadrilateral with opposite sides equal and 4 right angles

blocks.question: Tim says a square is NOT a rectangle. Is he right?
options: No — a square has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal, so it is a special rectangle
A square is a kind of triangle
blocks.explain: A rectangle is a four-sided shape with 4 right angles and opposite sides equal. A square has all of that — and its sides all happen to be equal too. So a square meets every rule for a rectangle; it is a special rectangle.
blocks.rule: A shape belongs to a group if it has all that group's properties.
blocks.principle: A square is a rectangle because it has every rectangle property (and more).
canonical_solution: A rectangle: 4 right angles, opposite sides equal
A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal
So a square meets all rectangle rules
A square is a special rectangle

rubric.look_for: lists the rectangle properties and checks the square
concludes a square qualifies as a rectangle

misconceptions.coach: Check the rules: a square has all four right angles and equal opposite sides.
Equal sides is extra, not a problem — a square is a special rectangle.

practiceItems.prompt: the number of right angles in a square
the number of sides on a square
the number of equal sides on a square

blocks.content: Sort triangles by equal sides, and remember any four-sided shape is a quadrilateral. Let's practise!
